Based on the given metrics and domain knowledge, we need to calculate the filesystem usage ratio for pods of the "ts-news-service" running on "k8s-node1" and "k8s-node4". To achieve this, we can use PromQL with the following logic:

1. Select the fs usage bytes for the relevant pods using `container_fs_usage_bytes`.
2. Select the fs limit bytes for the same pods using `container_fs_limit_bytes`.
3. Divide the usage bytes by the limit bytes for each pod to get the usage ratio.
4. Apply the condition to filter only those pods which belong to the "ts-news-service" and are hosted on "k8s-node1" or "k8s-node4".

Here's the PromQL query to achieve this:

```promql
(
  container_fs_usage_bytes{pod=~"ts-news-service-[a-zA-Z0-9]+[a-zA-Z0-9\-]*", node=~"k8s-node[14]"}
  /
  container_fs_limit_bytes{pod=~"ts-news-service-[a-zA-Z0-9]+[a-zA-Z0-9\-]*", node=~"k8s-node[14]"}
) * 100
```

This query selects both metrics for pods whose names match the pattern "ts-news-service-" followed by any alphanumeric characters and have the nodes either "k8s-node1" or "k8s-node4". It then calculates the percentage of usage by dividing usage bytes by limit bytes and multiplies by 100 to get the percentage value. Note that the regular expressions used (`~`) allow us to capture the varying pod names for the "ts-news-service".
